rotation.scope_note: Follow sources.json categories[marketing]._note. Keep a story only if AI is what makes it AND it touches buying or selling ads or selling products. Search counts only where paid placement is involved. Exclude pure SEO plumbing, general search features, moderation infra, publisher licensing, funding, M&A, hires, awards, vendor advertorials and agency-internal ops.

plan_notes: LIBRARIAN: (1) Lead with outlet RSS / sitemap_news.xml feeds for recency. Good starting points are ppc.land, digiday.com, adexchanger.com, adweek.com, marketingdive.com, seroundtable.com, searchenginejournal.com, modernretail.co, retaildive.com, techcrunch.com, blog.google (ads), about.fb.com, newsroom.tiktok.com and press.aboutamazon.com. Search Engine Land, Ad Age, The Drum, MediaPost, Marketing Brew and Campaign are hard-blocked, so get their stories through RSS or the same news covered by another outlet. Use WebSearch ONLY to fill gaps after the feeds, because site: search tends to return evergreen pages. (2) Window is 72h: keep items published 2026-10-11T00:00 to 2026-10-14 (KST) and verify each published time from the page. (3) Apply sources.json categories[marketing]._note scoping strictly. AI must make the story AND the story must touch ad buying/selling or product selling. If either is missing, drop it. Also drop SEO plumbing, funding/M&A/hires/awards and vendor advertorials. Read the body before keeping keyword-matched items, because advertorials pass keyword gates. (4) Skip the deprioritized stories listed above and only take follow-ups that report a new launch, data or decision. (5) Write candidates under the key "items".
